name: Maryland

sales.rateNote: General state sales and use tax of 6%, applied with a statutory bracket table (Tax-General 11-104). Since July 1, 2025 a separate 3% rate applies to data, IT and software publishing services (NAICS 518, 519, 5132, 5415). Other special rates: 9% alcoholic beverages, 12% cannabis, 8% peer-to-peer car sharing. Counties and cities cannot levy a sales tax.

local.levies: none: Tax-General 11-102(c) bars counties, municipalities and special taxing districts from imposing a retail sales or use tax (except taxes already in effect on January 1, 1971)

groceries.note: Food for consumption off the premises sold by a vendor operating a substantial grocery or market business is exempt; food for immediate consumption (heated food, salad bars, etc.) is taxable. Since July 1, 2025 vending-machine snack foods and cannabinoid beverages are no longer exempt.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxed at 6% except during the August back-to-school tax-free week (items of $100 or less).

otherRates.item: data, information technology and software publishing services (NAICS 518, 519, 5132, 5415)
otherRates.note: New taxable services from July 1, 2025 (Chapter 604 of the Acts of 2025).
6.5% of fair market value (3.5% for rental vehicles), collected at titling instead of sales tax.
60% on vaping liquid in containers of 5 ml or less; 12% on tobacco pipes.

holidays2026.name: Energy Star tax-free weekend
holidays2026.items: Energy Star air conditioners, clothes washers and dryers, furnaces, heat pumps, standard refrigerators, dehumidifiers, boilers, programmable thermostats, CFL bulbs, and solar water heaters

holidays2026.name: Back-to-school tax-free week
holidays2026.items: clothing and footwear priced $100 or less per item (accessories such as jewelry, watches and handbags excluded) and the first $40 of a backpack or bookbag

sales.holidayNote: Dates derived from the statutory rules: Saturday before the third Monday in February through that Monday; second Sunday in August through the following Saturday.

useTax.note: Maryland's tax is a combined sales and use tax at the same rates; it is due on taxable items bought without Maryland tax for use in the state.

facts.text: Since July 1, 2025 Maryland taxes data processing, web hosting, IT consulting and software publishing services at a reduced 3% rate.
The 2025 budget law repealed the sales tax exemptions for vending-machine snack foods and for bullion and coins sold for more than $1,000.
Cars pay a 6.5% excise tax at titling rather than the 6% sales tax.
State law prohibits Maryland counties and cities from creating their own sales tax, so 6% applies statewide.
Maryland has two tax-free periods a year: Energy Star appliances on Presidents' Day weekend and clothing under $100 in the second week of August.
The cannabis sales tax rose from 9% to 12% on July 1, 2025.

property.levied: state, counties (and Baltimore City) and municipalities; assessments are made by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)

assessment.text: Real property is revalued by physical inspection on a 3-year cycle; increases are phased in over the three years (one-third, two-thirds, then the full increase); if value has not increased, the most recent valuation applies.
assessment.capText: For an owner-occupied principal residence, the taxable assessment used for the State tax cannot rise more than 10% a year (homestead credit percentage of 110%); each county and Baltimore City sets its own cap between 0% and 10% (100%-110%), and municipalities may set theirs. Tax on any assessment increase above the cap is credited.

homestead.name: Homestead Tax Credit (assessment cap)
homestead.text: For an owner-occupied principal residence, the taxable assessment used for the State tax cannot rise more than 10% a year (homestead credit percentage of 110%); each county and Baltimore City sets its own cap between 0% and 10% (100%-110%), and municipalities may set theirs. Tax on any assessment increase above the cap is credited.
homestead.applyBy: One-time application to SDAT; the homeowner must reside in the dwelling by July 1 of the taxable year.

facts.text: Maryland caps yearly growth of a homeowner's taxable assessment at 10% for the State tax, and many counties choose a lower cap.
Counties and Baltimore City must set their homestead credit percentage by law before March 15 for the year starting July 1.
Assessment increases are phased in over a 3-year cycle: one-third of the increase each year.
Willful misrepresentation to obtain the homestead credit carries a penalty of 25% of the credit received in each year of non-qualification.
The Maryland property tax year runs from July 1 to June 30.

uncertain: The user brief mentions Maryland 'moving to 6%': the general rate is 6% (statutory bracket table); its original effective date (2008) was not read on an official page, effectiveSince left null. The 2025 change is the new 3% rate on IT/data services, verified.

SDAT (dat.maryland.gov) and MVA (mva.maryland.gov) return HTTP 403 to automated requests; property facts were taken from the Tax-Property Article on mgaleg.maryland.gov instead. Homeowners' Tax Credit (income-based) amounts, assessment ratio and payment due dates (July 1 bill, semiannual option) could not be read and are omitted.
Comptroller sales tax web pages (services.marylandcomptroller.gov) require JavaScript; statutes and the Comptroller's PDF alerts were used instead.
2026 holiday dates computed from the statutory rules, not from a Comptroller announcement.
